A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DenseVLM research. Text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material support reliable comparison despite the changed title, pagination and appendix numbering.

before.justification: v3 reports original dense representation experiments, downstream segmentation and detection results, scaling experiments, and main-text and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results, including benchmark comparisons, downstream task evaluations, scaling experiments and supplementary ablations.

M1.justification: The region retrieval, denoising, decoupled foreground/background alignment and KL-divergence training procedure are unchanged. Section 3 retains the same components and equations.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same COCO, ADE20K and SA-1B coverage, plus COCO-Stuff segmentation training, ADE-150/ADE-847 and PC-459 evaluation, and OV-COCO/OV-LVIS detection tasks.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main and supplementary experiments. Table 1 retains OpenCLIP, DFN, SigLIP, EVA-CLIP, RegionCLIP, FineCLIP and CLIPSelf; Tables 7 and 8 retain the same downstream comparators.

E3.justification: The reported splits, metrics, resolutions, backbones and training budgets match. The SA-1B scaling experiments retain the same 100K, 1.1M and 5.5M sample settings, and appendix training protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same analyses of framework design, decoupling, category sets, retrieval models, backbones, image resolution, region proposals and denoising thresholds. Confusion matrices and grid-patch classification examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Uncertainty reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Numerical results, plotted trends and qualitative examples match throughout the main text and supplement. For example, Table 1 retains DenseVLM's COCO Top1 accuracies of 72.3, 70.1 and 44.9 for boxes, thing masks and stuff masks, respectively.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(5), including retrieval probabilities, decoupled alignment distributions and the training loss, are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about foreground bias, DenseVLM alignment, downstream improvements and scalability. The new title emphasizes unbiased alignment already claimed in v3.

C2.justification: Interpretations of foreground bias, ablation outcomes and scalability are retained. Appendix A in v3 and supplementary Section 6 in v4 state the same limitations concerning computational resources, retrieval-model capacity and coarse thing/stuff semantics.

D1.justification: Implementation details, Table 9 hyperparameters, GPU information and downstream training schedules are unchanged. Both versions provide the same code repository; the revised availability sentence does not establish a resource change.

R1.justification: The same 75 reference entries and substantive related-work discussion are retained. Bibliography relocation and updated citation page references do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'DenseVLM: A Retrieval and Decoupled Alignment Framework for Open-Vocabulary Dense Prediction' to 'Unbiased Region-Language Alignment for Open-Vocabulary Dense Prediction.' Author and affiliation text receive small edits, references move before the supplement, and appendix sections A–E become Sections 6–10. Substantive prose is otherwise retained.

P2.justification: Typesetting and spacing changes reflow text and equations, and printed page numbers disappear. The bibliography becomes contiguous before the supplement instead of being interrupted by supplementary figures. All 14 tables and 11 figures retain their content and display structure.

improvement.justification: v4 mainly retitles and reformats the same paper. Collecting the bibliography before the supplement provides a small organizational benefit, but the method, empirical evidence, explanations, limitations and reproducibility information remain unchanged. These presentation edits do not establish a meaningful overall quality difference.
